item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-c8782debda6d3da5","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"A nationally representative IRI survey conducted March–April 2023 found 70% approval of Sheikh Hasina’s performance, but only 44% believed Bangladesh was headed in the right direction, down from 76% in 2019; rising prices were the primary source of pessimism.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2023; survey fieldwork preceded publication.","ruler_attribution":"The survey reports public approval and dissatisfaction during Hasina’s premiership but does not establish causal responsibility for all economic conditions.","limitations":["Survey perceptions are not independent evidence of policy implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c8782debda6d3da5","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The 2023 IRI survey reported growing opposition support, with approval of the opposition rising to 63%, and found that respondents wanted improved electoral transparency and fairness; 44% supported restoring a caretaker-government election system, while 92% said they were likely to vote.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.8","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns the 2023 pre-election environment.","ruler_attribution":"The findings describe public demands and perceived electoral barriers under Hasina’s government, without independently attributing each barrier to her personally.","limitations":["The source is a survey and does not document specific administrative or legal acts."]},{"source_id":"SRC-841287b77d972dd7","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Amnesty’s Bangladesh country page states that the Cyber Security Act of 2023 continued the restrictive framework of the Digital Security Act; its urgent-action listings identify a student detained for organizing a webinar and a journalist detained while reporting on rising living costs in 2023.","question_ids":["3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Cyber Security Act and the listed detentions directly concern 2023, although the page is a later retrospective.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct occurred under Hasina’s government, but the page does not identify her personal orders in these cases.","limitations":["The extracted page provides limited case detail and does not establish final judicial outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35a06d1974b8a5d7","start_unit":3,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reports that before the January 2024 election, security forces arrested tens of thousands of opposition members and supporters; opposition parties boycotted the polls, and the United States, United Kingdom, and UN said the process was not inclusive. It also reports that Hasina’s administration targeted activists, journalists, and political dissidents through arbitrary arrests and surveillance, and that the 2023 Cyber Security Act retained broad powers to criminalize and imprison political critics.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.5","3B.8","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","4B.9","7B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The election repression occurred in the late-2023 pre-election period and the CSA was enacted in 2023; the report was published in 2025 and partly describes 2024 events.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes sustained repression and institutional control to Hasina’s administration, while specific arrests are attributed to security forces.","limitations":["Some described events occurred in 2024 rather than 2023; the source is retrospective."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35a06d1974b8a5d7","start_unit":5,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reports that under Hasina, enforced disappearances and torture allegations persisted: Odhikar estimated more than 700 enforced disappearances, nearly 100 people remained missing, and released detainees described solitary confinement and hearing other detainees being tortured; it also reports widespread gender-based violence, limited access to justice, high child marriage, and criminalization of same-sex conduct.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.7","3B.10","6B.3","6B.8","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report describes patterns during Hasina’s 15-year administration, including conditions relevant to 2023, but does not isolate 2023 figures.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the disappearance pattern to the Hasina government while noting that allegations were rarely investigated or prosecuted.","limitations":["The figures are estimates and retrospective; direct 2023 attribution and year-specific trends are limited."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35a06d1974b8a5d7","start_unit":6,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reports that Bangladesh made economic progress but experienced uneven resource distribution, very high youth unemployment—42% among young women—and a decade-high cost of living; it also reports labor protests over wages, police use of tear gas, dangerous and underregulated shipbreaking, and incomplete labor-law protections.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The report concerns 2024 but describes structural and economic conditions inherited from the Hasina period, including issues relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source identifies structural conditions and government shortcomings but does not assign all outcomes personally to Hasina.","limitations":["Most indicators are not year-specific to 2023 and include post-Hasina developments."]},{"source_id":"SRC-71a66634d1204322","start_unit":3,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"Freedom House states that the Awami League consolidated political power through sustained harassment of opposition actors and critical media and by co-opting state institutions during Hasina’s 15 years in power; it rates Bangladesh Partly Free and reports that the 2024 election followed this pattern.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.5","4B.6","4B.8","4B.10","7B.6","8B.5","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source is a 2026 country profile with a retrospective assessment covering Hasina’s 15-year rule, including 2023; the 2024 election is outside the target period but evidences continuity.","ruler_attribution":"Freedom House attributes the consolidation to the ruling Awami League and Hasina-era administration rather than documenting only her personal acts.","limitations":["The extracted profile does not provide a year-specific 2023 score or event inventory."]},{"source_id":"SRC-71a66634d1204322","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Freedom House reports that Bangladesh had restricted networks, blocked social media and websites, pro-government commentators, and arrested users; it lists the January 7, 2024 parliamentary election as occurring after the Hasina-era political environment.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The internet-freedom indicators are from a later profile and are not explicitly dated to 2023; the election reference is 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The profile concerns the national governing environment associated with the Awami League, but does not establish that every listed restriction was ordered by Hasina.","limitations":["Insufficient date specificity for direct 2023 attribution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9a31c24e4b60e94e","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"ACLED reports that Sheikh Hasina was re-elected in January 2024 for a fourth consecutive term after the BNP opposition boycott; the AL won 225 of 300 seats, turnout was disputed, hundreds were reportedly injured, at least eight people were killed, and thousands of opposition activists were arrested or detained before the vote.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.9","4B.10","8B.5","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The source concerns January 2024, but the arrests, demonstrations, and electoral conditions occurred in the late-2023 to early-2024 period.","ruler_attribution":"The report describes the governing party and state authorities during Hasina’s re-election campaign; it does not prove her personal direction of each arrest or violent incident.","limitations":["The election itself falls outside 2023; turnout and violence figures are reported or disputed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-02a475121cf52f55","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"ACLED reports that Hasina resigned and fled on August 5, 2024 after weeks of deadly demonstrations; the protests began over a quota policy widely viewed as patronage for ruling-party affiliates, escalated after she called demonstrators Razakar sympathizers, and were met with live ammunition, rubber bullets, tear gas, a curfew, communications blackout, army deployment, and mass arrests.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","4B.2","4B.3","4B.9","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns 2024, outside the 2023–2023 target period; it may provide only later evidence about the durability of Hasina-era practices.","ruler_attribution":"ACLED attributes the escalation partly to Hasina’s characterization of protesters and to government and security-force actions.","limitations":["This is outside the target period and should not be treated as direct 2023 evidence."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-f78c5d3f509f4c69","SRC-4dc5746e0f0d1f30","SRC-049815ac899a0c8b","SRC-bc26b847ed226c7f","SRC-ffc215e0d1c8e802","SRC-112d13787e024336"],"batch_limitations":["Several supplied documents concern 2024–2026 and provide only retrospective or contextual evidence for the 2023 target period.","The supplied material is concentrated on political freedom, domestic safety, human rights, and economic conditions; it contains no material evidence on nuclear risk and little direct evidence on international peace, ruler integrity, or administrative effectiveness.","No scores are assigned."]}
